question: Should OpenClaw accept the temporary shared Kotlin 2.4.0 pin after the pending Android build/test checks pass, or require a CodeQL-scoped workaround that leaves ordinary Android builds on 2.4.10?
rationale: The PR intentionally changes the compiler version used by all Android builds to repair one security-analysis workflow; repository policy treats this kind of shared compatibility change as a maintainer-visible upgrade and automation decision.

options.title: Land after Android validation
options.body: Accept the temporary shared pin if the exact-head Android build and test jobs complete successfully, then track restoration when CodeQL supports Kotlin 2.4.10.

options.title: Require a CodeQL-only workaround
options.body: Keep Android builds on Kotlin 2.4.10 and revise the security workflow only if the shared pin causes compatibility or maintenance concerns.

recommendation.title: Land after Android validation
recommendation.body: Accept the temporary shared pin if the exact-head Android build and test jobs complete successfully, then track restoration when CodeQL supports Kotlin 2.4.10.

likelyOwner.reason: The MEMBER author is currently assigned and supplied the CodeQL compatibility evidence; additional Android-area ownership could not be established without local history access.
